blocking_findings: The future-change experiment does not establish an NBO work-to-accuracy advantage: adaptive NBO is more expensive than fresh NBO refitting in all eight cells and SAA is the least-cost fully certified service in all eight.
The signed economic comparative statics are valid but are not unlocked by NBO; full-support enumeration gives the same finite-law target more sharply and at lower cost than adaptive NBO.

The policy-composition theorem is a correct conditional bridge but is not instantiated with uniform state coverage, class approximation, value transfer, and implementation allowances for the broad applications.
The experimental problem remains a short-horizon, sixteen-atom, scalar-action finite service despite state dimensions ten and fifty.
The analytical amortization result applies to generic fixed-feature regression and does not establish the property for the jointly trained neural continuation.
Three fixed streams and finite task catalogues certify listed services but do not support a method-level reliability statement over training randomness or economic tasks.
The decisive prospective numerical tests are not carried through recursive utility, endogenous preferences, temporal selves, or strategic games.
The 51-page article, 232-page supplement, and 48-page applications companion remain disproportionate to the narrow result established by the new evidence.
The principal economic counterfactual is stylized, uses a specified rather than reoptimized future policy, and does not yet supply an Econometrica-scale substantive result.
limitations: The reviewer did not rerun the original fitting jobs; a new execution would not reproduce the original measured clocks.
The reviewer did not rerun the full 1,292-second field-by-field certificate replay; that exhaustive result is taken from the committed release audit.
The reviewer independently verified the final artifact digest, all 210 publication file hashes, unit tests, committed aggregate calculations, and the original R20 source-and-evidence package.
No claim is made that a failed certificate proves excessive actual loss, or that finite fixed-stream comparisons establish population performance.
This advisory review is not an Econometric Society editorial decision.
positive_findings: R21 genuinely tests changes in future policy, production technology, and valuation rather than only identical-future reuse.
The true-objective scalar-interval stopping certificate and complete work accounting are credible and method neutral.
The policy-composition theorem correctly identifies own-policy continuation, uniform domain coverage, and propagation weights.
The NBO action-radius bands yield valid negative finite-law withdrawal responses to stronger future production and valuation.
Adverse results, failed reuse checks, conventional competitors, and unfavorable cost frontiers are preserved.
The source-bound publication, preservation record, test suite, and arithmetic audit are exceptionally strong.
recommendation: Reject in the present form and do not continue the cumulative manuscript through another ordinary revision round; encourage a new, substantially shorter submission centered on certified continuation services or on a setting with a demonstrated neural work-to-accuracy advantage.
